name: Spades
description:
Spades

    enumi1

  1. Sheepwalk Ledge — Goat path with room for one honest lie at a time. `[THRESHOLD]` `[OATH]`

    The lie must be about an oath you broke. Tell it, and the ledge holds. Refuse, and the path crumbles—start a Fallen Kin [4] timer (the ancestor whose oath you broke is watching). The ledge is eight paces long. Do not take a ninth.

    Guest-right cost: If you cross without offering a pinch of salt to the cairn at the far end, the ledge becomes Desperate for all navigation rolls.

    Blood-price: 1 cow (if the ledge collapses on someone, that is the blood-price).

  2. Warden's Cairn — Windy tor; signal-fire basket and dry cache; eyes of the hills. `[WATCH]`

    The cache holds a single arrow. Light it with the fire, and the message is war. The arrow is fletched with eagle feathers—a clan's highest oath. The cairn has eight faces. The ninth is hidden.

    Guest-right cost: Asking for shelter here requires you to name a weight you still carry. If you refuse, the Warden marks you—start Suspicion [4].

    Blood-price: 2 cows (the cost of a false alarm).

  3. Wergild Ford — Flat stones, deep pools, table rock for counting silver. `[LAW]` `[TRADE]`

    The table rock is smooth as glass. Blood washes off; lies do not. The water remembers every price ever paid here. The ford has eight crossings. The ninth is the Hollow's.

    Blood-prices paid here are witnessed by the stones. If you cross without paying a due weight, the water rises—test Body+Athletics (DV 4) or lose 1 Supply (drowned cargo).

  4. Droppers' Bridge — Stone span rigged to fall; pins already loosened. `[TRAP]`

    The pins are greased with mutton fat. The bridge knows who paid for the grease. Its fall has ended three feuds and started two. There are eight pins. The ninth is a story.

    Crossing cost: Spend 1 Boon or mark 1 Fatigue to notice the loosened pins (Wits+Notice DV 3). On a Miss, the bridge drops—test Body+Athletics or take Harm 1.

  5. Scree-Ladder — Climbing to a notch; red rags mark safe steps through danger. `[TRAVEL]`

    The rags are old clan banners. Step where they wave, not where they lie flat. One rag is white—that marks a traitor's grave. There are eight ladders. The ninth is a fall.

    Guest-right cost: A guide demands a story before showing you the safe route. If you refuse, the ladder becomes Desperate for all climbing rolls.

  6. Moot Hollow — Ring of standing stones; voices carry and won't quite stop. `[SOCIAL]` `[OATH]`

    The stones have ears. Speak a false oath here, and every cairn will know. The dead vote by how the mist moves. There are eight stones. The ninth is the space between.

    Cairn vote: Any oath sworn here is witnessed by the stones. Break it, and the cairns vote against you automatically (see Cairn Vote table).

  7. Reiver's Gate — Between boulders; cart-ruts vanish into heather's memory. `[STEALTH]`

    The gate has no lintel. Above it, ravens nest in a skull. The ravens are the clan's spies. They count in caws—never more than eight.

    Passing cost: The ravens demand a secret. Tell a true secret, and they let you pass unseen. Refuse, and they raise the alarm—start Watch Patrol [4].

  8. Khaz-Vurim Steps — Dwarf-cut switchbacks with iron mile studs; toll and toil. `[TRAVEL]` `[AUTHORITY]`

    The studs are cold iron. Touch them, and the mountain knows your weight. Aeler outcasts maintain the toll—they accept stories as often as coin. They count in eights. If you hear a ninth, run.

    Toll: 1 Supply or a story that makes the toll-keeper laugh. If you cannot pay, you are turned back—lose 1 segment of progress.

  9. Gray Tor Fort — Earthen rampart, timber crown, smoky cook pits. `[COMMUNITY]`

    The cook pits have been burning for three hundred years. The ash is deep enough to bury a secret—and more than one Viterran scout. The fort has eight gates. The ninth is a wall.

    Guest-right cost: To enter the fort, you must share a meal. Refusing starts a Grudge of the Hearth [4] timer.

    J
    Black Broom Bog — Stepping-logs; wrong one drinks you into silence. `[DEATH]` `[FEAR]`

    The logs are painted with warding runes. One is unpainted—that one is the quick way. The bog exhales names of the drowned. There are eight logs. The ninth is a whisper.

    Cairn vote: The bog is sacred to the dead. Any violence here triggers a cairn vote. The dead always vote for war (advance the nearest Feud timer by +2).

    Q
    Bride's Causey — Raised road to a valley kirk; ribbons hang like warnings. `[SOCIAL]`

    The ribbons are from wedding gowns—cut short when the groom fell in a feud. The kirk is neutral ground, but the path is not. The causey has eight spans. The ninth is a promise.

    Guest-right cost: To cross, you must accept a cup of water from the bride's kin. Refusal is an insult—start Bride-Price Default [4].

    K
    Three-Fires Ridge — Watchposts that see Viterra and Vhasia both; news travels fast. `[WATCH]`

    The fires are layered: birch for peace, pine for raid, oak for invasion. A fourth fire—yew—means the Hollow walks. The watchmen count in eights. The ninth signal is never sent.

    Using the fires: A successful Wits+Lore (DV 3) lets you read the beacon code and learn the state of the passes. On a Miss, you misread the signals—start False Alarm [4].

    A
    Pass of Ashes — When snow closes here, the upland becomes an island. `[WEATHER]` `[DEATH]`

    The ash is from old sacrifices. The pass remembers every offering. The last sacrifice was a Viterran herald. His voice is still in the wind. The pass has eight turns. The ninth is a cairn.

    Cairn vote: The pass is watched by the ghost of the herald. Any oath sworn here is witnessed by the dead. Break it, and the cairn votes for war automatically.
